hook: In Russia, twenty four thousand, seven hundred and fifty one villages have no one left. Not a single person.
noroad: Many villages that are still alive have no real road out. In 2011, the government itself said forty six thousand villages had no road you could use all year.
ice: So in winter, people drive on ice. In Yakutia alone, crews open more than eleven thousand kilometres of winter roads, across frozen rivers and swamps. In spring, they simply melt away.
yakutia: Yakutia is bigger than Argentina, and about ninety percent of it has no year round transport at all.
delivery: About eighteen hundred Arctic settlements wait for one big delivery a year. Fuel and food come by barge or helicopter, before the ice closes in.
end: Out here, life runs on seasons, not schedules. Would you live somewhere you can only reach when the river freezes?
